You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is a frog visibly present inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly shows a frog within the toilet bowl; fail if the bowl is visible and no frog is inside it; unknown if the bowl or its contents cannot be assessed reliably.
node.binding: Assess the frog’s placement relative to the toilet bowl in the image, using the toilet in the input image as the reference. A frog elsewhere does not satisfy this check.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive: it treats s1’s claim that a frog is inside the bowl as sufficient, and the downstream trace simply repeats that claim. In the edited image, one frog is visibly in the bowl, but additional frogs are on the raised lid/tank area and on the floor; this is clear partial progress, not full fulfillment of “Put a frog in the toilet” if the requested edit is judged as a whole. Make the decision explicitly compare the edited image with the source and assess all requested placement evidence, distinguishing a frog inside the bowl from frogs merely on the toilet exterior or nearby. Do not let a positive support observation or high confidence substitute for inspecting the image and applying the rubric’s partial-progress rule. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient evidence; this trace shows no transport, schema, or dependency failure to explain the disagreement.
s2: The node is a support/evidence check, not the fulfillment decision, so keep its scope distinct: it should report whether the bowl is assessable and what visible placement evidence exists, rather than infer completion from s1’s positive claim. Its current binding is too narrow and permits the downstream check to echo “frog inside” as sufficient. Have it inspect the edited image directly and, where available, compare with the source; distinguish frogs inside the bowl from frogs on the lid/tank or nearby, and pass those observations onward so the fulfillment criterion can apply the rubric’s partial-progress rule. Here the edited image shows a frog in the bowl plus frogs on the raised toilet area and floor, while the source has no visible frogs; that is progress but does not by itself establish full fulfillment. Preserve unknown only when visibility is genuinely insufficient. The trace shows valid execution and dependencies, so address semantic scope and evidence routing, not transport or schema.

In this example the source has no frogs; the edit adds one in the bowl and others on the raised toilet area and floor.
